headline: A fairly strong cold front brings intense bursts of rain, gusty winds and a small chance of thunderstorms to San Diego County Thursday afternoon, with possible street flooding, before dry, cool weather returns Friday through the weekend.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday is fair but cool after a chilly start, with highs in the mid 60s to lower 70s at lower elevations, about 1–3 degrees below average at the coast and 4–10 degrees below average in the valleys. Some patchy low clouds this morning up to about 20 miles inland give way to high clouds building in this afternoon and evening ahead of the next storm. Lower clouds thicken overnight, and a Wind Advisory begins at 11 PM for the San Bernardino County Mountains and the Apple and Lucerne Valleys.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thursday's storm will be fairly strong, with a well-defined cold front bringing rain to the L.A. Basin in the morning (around 8–10 AM in Orange County) and moving southeast into Riverside and San Diego Counties in the afternoon, reaching the San Diego area around 11 AM–1 PM. Rain will be intense along the front with a small chance of thunderstorms, and rates of 0.50–0.65 inch per hour could cause some urban flooding; gusts top 25–30 mph at the coast and 40–55 mph in the mountains and desert slopes, where the Wind Advisory runs until 4 PM Thursday. Snow levels start high and fall to about 6,500 feet, with a few inches above 7,500 feet on the upper Big Bear ski slopes but little if any at Big Bear Lake; showers follow Thursday evening and end Thursday night. Friday starts quite cold but turns mostly sunny, and light offshore (easterly) winds Friday night into Saturday will be brisk only in a few isolated foothill spots.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Friday through the weekend stay dry and slightly warmer but still below normal, with highs in the mid 60s to lower 70s at lower elevations, upper 30s to mid 50s in the mountains, and 50s in the High Desert. A much weaker disturbance arrives Sunday, bringing light showers Sunday night and Monday with far less rain and wind than Thursday's storm. By Tuesday the computer models are split almost evenly between continued unsettled, occasionally wet and windy weather and a drier, warmer pattern heading into the Thanksgiving holiday.

coast: Surf eases to 3–5 feet today as the shorter-period northwest swell fades, leaving a 3–5 ft swell every 13–14 seconds. A new northwest swell builds Thursday, raising surf again Thursday evening into early Friday. Coastal flooding is expected at times through the rest of the week; King Tides peak next week, with tides above 7 feet possible as early as Saturday, Nov. 21. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory runs from 4 AM Thursday to 10 AM Friday with steep 7–10 ft seas and 20–30 knot gusts, winds turning from south-southwest to west by late Thursday afternoon; conditions improve later Friday and seas are much calmer by the weekend.
watch_for: Heavy downpours of 0.50–0.65 inch per hour along Thursday afternoon's front, with possible urban flooding and a small chance of thunderstorms.
How much snow falls in the San Bernardino Mountains Thursday, since the timing of the cold air is uncertain.
Whether the pattern stays unsettled or turns dry and warmer heading into the Thanksgiving holiday.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in Thursday's storm and a dry, cool Friday through Sunday, less certain about mountain snow amounts, and evenly split on the pattern from Tuesday into the holiday.
